implementationPlan.description: RECEIPT MODULE, TDD under the ROOT lane (the security lane excludes `*.test.ts`, so the unit test runs with `pnpm exec vitest run tests/security/lane-receipts.test.ts`). RED FIRST: create tests/security/lane-receipts.test.ts importing from "./lane-receipts.js" (does not exist yet). Then create tests/security/lane-receipts.ts (NOT a `*.security.ts` file — the lane would collect it as an empty suite; same reason hostile-harness.ts carries no suffix; target ≤ 200 lines): (1) a FROZEN diagnostic roster `SECURITY_COVERAGE_DIAGNOSTICS = ["SECURITY_COVERAGE_UNEXECUTED_REGISTRATION", "SECURITY_COVERAGE_DUPLICATE_SLICE_RECEIPT", "SECURITY_COVERAGE_DUPLICATE_BOUNDARY_CLAIM", "SECURITY_COVERAGE_FOREIGN_BOUNDARY", "SECURITY_COVERAGE_FOREIGN_RUN", "SECURITY_COVERAGE_MISSING_SLICE_RECEIPT", "SECURITY_COVERAGE_MISSING_ARM"]` and a `CoverageDiagnostic` error class carrying `{ code, detail }`; (2) `writeSliceReceipt(dir, receipt)` — receipt = `{ runId, sliceFile, entries: [{ boundary, arm, caseId }] }`, written ATOMICALLY (write `<sliceFile>.json.tmp` then `renameSync`), refusing `DUPLICATE_SLICE_RECEIPT` if `<sliceFile>.json` already exists in `dir` and `UNEXECUTED_REGISTRATION` if any entry's `caseId` is empty; (3) `readSliceReceipts(dir, runId)` — refusing `FOREIGN_RUN` on a receipt whose runId differs; (4) `resolveExecutedCoverage({ receipts, sliceFiles, roster })` returning `{ pairs, diagnostics }` where diagnostics enumerate MISSING_SLICE_RECEIPT (a listed slice file with no receipt — never executed), FOREIGN_BOUNDARY (a boundary outside `roster`), DUPLICATE_BOUNDARY_CLAIM (one boundary in two slices' receipts), MISSING_ARM (`<BOUNDARY>#<ARM>` for each roster boundary lacking BEFORE, AFTER or RACE); pure functions, no vitest import. Arms in the test: roster has 7 unique nonzero entries; each diagnostic is producible by exactly one constructed input and carries its code; atomic write leaves no `.tmp` behind; a happy path with two slices and three arms resolves zero diagnostics and the exact pair set. Run → RED on the missing module, then GREEN; quote counts.

implementationPlan.description: DRILLS (DoD 4) — each alone, restore before the next; all mutated paths are TRACKED, so `git status --porcelain <path>` before and `git diff --exit-code -- <path>` after prove the restore. Mutate a CASES module in the runtime-provider axis (e.g. tests/security/runtime-provider-benchmark-cases.ts:62 `ledger.refused(BOUNDARY, "AFTER", outcome.effect, …)`): (a) DELETE that AFTER registration → completeness reds `SECURITY_COVERAGE_MISSING_ARM` naming `<that boundary>#AFTER` (if a sibling registration on the same boundary+arm keeps it green, pick a boundary with exactly one AFTER site and say so); (b) COMMENT OUT the registration (`// ledger.refused(…)`) → the same named red — the old scanner credited this, the receipt cannot; (c) move the registration behind `if (false) { … }` or after a `return` → the same named red; (d) PUSH OUTSIDE A TEST: add a `ledger.refused(…)` call at module scope of one slice → the receipt write refuses `SECURITY_COVERAGE_UNEXECUTED_REGISTRATION` and completeness reds `SECURITY_COVERAGE_MISSING_SLICE_RECEIPT` for that slice; (e) FOREIGN: register a boundary name not in the roster → `SECURITY_COVERAGE_FOREIGN_BOUNDARY`. Confirm each mutation actually landed before rerunning, and that the arm/diagnostic that reds is the one whose name claims that behaviour. A GREEN drill is a FINDING to disclose, not a pass.
